consensus_summary: Consensus primary identification of 'the truth' is Jesus Christ as the personal embodiment of God's self-revelation and divine reality, with complementary secondary layers including Scripture/word, gospel/doctrine, Spirit of truth, and God's faithfulness.
book_summary: The book identifies 'the truth' as God's law — the standard.
boundary_disagreement: Book centers exclusively on God's law as the referent; consensus treats law/Scripture only as a secondary or alternative layer while centering Christ, so the book excludes the Christological primary cases that consensus admits as core.
material_contradiction: The book's core (truth = God's law) cannot hold as the identification in the same sense if the consensus core (truth = Christ himself) is retained; accepting the book requires replacing the consensus primary referent.
rationale: Minimum cores are non-equivalent: consensus responses A/B/C all fix Christ (via John 14:6 and related Johannine texts) as the settled primary while listing law/word only among alternatives; the book instead installs God's law as the entry itself and explicitly flags the Christ/gospel reading as the common view. This is referent replacement, not a boundary adjustment around a shared category.
strongest_objection: Ps 119:142 (shared with consensus alternatives) supports 'law is truth' but does not displace the dominant Christocentric consensus that the book itself acknowledges as commonly taught.
